title: Oxford Case Histories in Gastroenterology and Hepatology
author: Alissa J. Walsh and Colleagues
summary: Fifty real cases from Oxford gastroenterology practice, written for specialty trainees preparing for exit examinations and for consultants revalidating. Each case gives a brief history and investigations, followed by questions on differential diagnosis and management with detailed, evidence-based answers. Topics range across luminal, liver and pancreatic disease, from variceal bleeding, autoimmune hepatitis and Wilson's disease to Crohn's disease, coeliac disease, intestinal tuberculosis and refeeding syndrome. Cases are indexed by diagnosis, presenting features and aetiological mechanism.

title: Pancreatitis and Its Complications
author: Chris E. Forsmark
summary: Seventeen chapters by pancreatologists, endoscopists and surgeons, in two parts. The acute pancreatitis part covers epidemiology and pathophysiology, diagnosis and risk stratification, gallstone and other causes, treatment of mild and severe disease, prevention of post-ERCP pancreatitis, necrosis and infection, and fluid collections and pseudocysts. The chronic pancreatitis part covers epidemiology, genetic and other risk factors, natural history, diagnosis, pain management, endoscopic and surgical treatment, exocrine insufficiency and complications. Intended for clinicians and for scientists wanting a clinical background, as part of the Clinical Gastroenterology series.

title: Practical Algorithms in Pediatric Gastroenterology
author: Ron Shaoul
summary: A short book of diagnostic flowcharts for common problems in children's gastroenterology, part of Karger's Practical Algorithms in Pediatrics series. Each topic fills a two-page spread, with a decision algorithm on one side and brief explanatory notes on the other. Sections cover general presentations such as abdominal pain, diarrhoea and bleeding, reflux and vomiting, motility disorders, the stomach and intestine, inflammatory bowel disease, surgical conditions, the liver and the pancreas. Aimed at paediatricians, trainees and paediatric gastroenterologists.

title: Autoimmune Hepatitis
subtitle: A Guide for Practicing Clinicians
author: Gideon M. Hirschfield and E. Jenny Heathcote
summary: Thirteen chapters by North American and European contributors take autoimmune hepatitis from pathogenesis and clinical presentation through serological diagnosis and its drug-induced and immune-mediated mimics. Separate chapters cover when and how to treat adults and children, second-line therapy for non-responders, liver transplantation, pregnancy, treatment side effects and overlap syndromes with other autoimmune liver diseases. Written for gastroenterologists and hepatologists managing these patients in routine practice, it belongs to the Clinical Gastroenterology series.

title: Get ahead! Medicine
subtitle: 300 SBAs for Finals
author: Hiruni Jayasena and Colleagues
summary: Six practice papers of 50 single best answer questions each, written for UK medical students preparing for finals and modelled on the Medical Schools Council Assessment Alliance question bank. Each paper is followed by its answers, which explain the reasoning and add a short summary of the topic. Questions span the finals medicine syllabus, including cardiology, respiratory, gastroenterology and liver disease, neurology, endocrinology, dermatology, infection and statistics, with some harder stems for students aiming for honours. An index of topics closes the book.

title: Viral Hepatitis
subtitle: Chronic Hepatitis C
author: Resat Ozaras and Dominique Salmon-Ceron
summary: A concise clinical guide to hepatitis C in the era of interferon-free direct-acting antivirals. Eleven chapters cover global epidemiology, laboratory and molecular diagnosis with resistance testing, pre-treatment evaluation and current therapy for treatment-naive patients. Later chapters address special situations: renal failure, HBV coinfection, people who inject drugs and prisoners, HIV coinfection, failure of direct-acting antiviral therapy, decompensated cirrhosis and transplantation, extrahepatic manifestations and acute hepatitis C. It is written for specialists and for generalists who will screen and treat patients.

title: Oxford American Handbook of Gastroenterology and Hepatology
author: Adam S. Cheifetz and Colleagues
summary: A pocket handbook in the Oxford note format, with most topics on a two-page spread, written for medical students, residents and gastroenterology fellows. It opens with the ten most common clinical problems, such as anaemia with occult bleeding and ascites, and with gastrointestinal emergencies, then works by organ through the oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, liver, pancreas and biliary tree, and colon and rectum. Later chapters cover intestinal infections, gastrointestinal features of systemic disease, endoscopic procedures and nutrition, followed by an appendix and colour plates.

title: Management of Wilson Disease
subtitle: A Pocket Guide
author: Michael L. Schilsky
summary: A pocket-sized guide to Wilson disease in fourteen chapters, edited by Michael L. Schilsky of Yale. It moves from copper metabolism, diagnostic confirmation and family screening through treatment options, dietary copper, and the management of hepatic, neurological and psychiatric features. Later chapters cover treatment monitoring, children and other special circumstances, liver transplantation, research participation, and the social and emotional impact on patients and families, partly written with the Wilson Disease Association. Suited to hepatologists, neurologists and general physicians.

title: Clinic Handbook of Gastroenterology
author: John L.H. Wong and Colleagues
summary: A practical guide to the gastroenterology outpatient clinic, written by a team at the Royal Cornwall Hospital for senior house officers and specialist registrars. The early chapters take a symptom-based approach to investigation: dyspepsia, dysphagia, jaundice, iron deficiency anaemia, rectal bleeding, abdominal pain, abnormal liver tests, change in bowel habit and weight loss. Later chapters cover screening, IBD, IBS, chronic viral and non-viral liver disease, coeliac disease and nutrition, followed by service development, patient information, teaching, quality assurance, radiology and palliation of GI symptoms.

title: The Internist's Guide to Minimally Invasive Gastrointestinal Surgery
author: Craig Rezac and Kristen Donohue
summary: Twelve chapters, part of the Clinical Gastroenterology series, that explain laparoscopic, robotic and endoscopic GI surgery to physicians who refer patients for it. After an introduction to the history and benefits of minimally invasive surgery and a chapter on endoscopic interventions, the book moves organ by organ: benign and malignant oesophageal disease, gallbladder, liver, pancreas, small bowel, colorectal polyps and cancer, volvulus and diverticulitis, and hernia repair. Each chapter addresses patient selection, expected recovery and limitations, and contraindications to a minimally invasive approach.

title: Colorectal Cancer Screening
subtitle: Theory and Practical Application
author: Han-Mo Chiu and Hsiu-Hsi Chen
summary: Eleven chapters drawn from more than two decades of running the Taiwanese Colorectal Cancer Screening Program. They cover the epidemiology and risk factors of colorectal cancer, organised population-based screening, the choice of screening test, colonoscopy-based and non-invasive stool testing, health information systems and quality assurance. Later chapters turn to screening theory: short-term evaluation, mathematical modelling beyond randomised trials, cost-effectiveness analysis, and personalised risk-based screening in the big data era. Written for gastroenterologists, colonoscopists, primary care doctors, public health workers and programme planners.

title: Viral Hepatitis in Children
subtitle: Unique Features and Opportunities
author: Maureen M. Jonas
summary: A short edited volume in the Clinical Gastroenterology series, written for paediatricians, paediatric gastroenterologists, hepatologists and infectious disease specialists. Nine chapters cover hepatitis A, the epidemiology, natural history and treatment of hepatitis B and C in children, hepatitis D and E, and hepatitis caused by non-A to E viruses. Further chapters address immunoprophylaxis against hepatitis A and B, and the primary care diagnosis, monitoring and general management of children with viral hepatitis.

title: Emergencies in Gastroenterology and Hepatology
author: Daniel Marks and Marcus Harbord
summary: A pocket guide from the Oxford Emergencies in... series for managing acutely unwell gastroenterology and liver patients at the bedside. Its 22 chapters move from upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding, severe anaemia, vomiting, diarrhoea, gastroenteritis and complications of inflammatory bowel disease to acute abdominal and thoracic pain, nutrition, HIV, jaundice, acute liver failure, complications of cirrhosis, drug-induced liver injury, liver disease in pregnancy, hepatic trauma and liver transplant patients. Advice is practical and set out in short bulleted sections for trainees and acute physicians.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
subtitle: Diagnosis and Therapeutics
author: Russell D. Cohen
summary: Nineteen chapters edited by Russell D. Cohen of the University of Chicago, in the Clinical Gastroenterology series. Opening chapters trace the history of IBD therapy, its changing epidemiology, genetics and pathogenesis. The core reviews medical treatment in adults, with separate chapters on mesalamine, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, biological therapies, and probiotics, antibiotics and nutrition. Later chapters address paediatric IBD, surgery, serological markers and thiopurine monitoring, women with IBD, imaging and newer diagnostic techniques, a pathology slideshow, colorectal cancer surveillance, faecal diversion and the economics of IBD.

title: Bile Acids in Gastroenterology
subtitle: Basic and Clinical
author: Susumu Tazuma and Hajime Takikawa
summary: Japanese clinicians and scientists, edited by Susumu Tazuma and Hajime Takikawa, review bile acids from biochemistry to the clinic. Part I covers bile acid metabolism, hepatobiliary transport, intestinal digestion and absorption, nuclear receptor regulation and bile acids as therapeutic agents. Part II links bile acids to disease: gallstones, primary biliary cholangitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, inborn errors of bile acid synthesis, NAFLD and NASH, viral hepatitis and hepatocellular carcinoma, pancreatic disease, oesophageal and colorectal cancer, and metabolic syndrome. Useful for hepatologists, gastroenterologists and researchers.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Capsule Endoscopy
subtitle: A Gamechanger for a Groundbreaking Technique
author: Miguel Mascarenhas and Colleagues
summary: Fifteen chapters on how machine learning and deep learning are being applied to capsule endoscopy. Opening chapters explain AI basics, capsule types and the clinical indications, including obscure GI bleeding and Crohn's disease. The core chapters review AI detection of blood, ulcers and erosions, protruding lesions, vascular lesions and luminal content, followed by bowel cleansing, blockchain for data storage, magnetic capsules, virtual chromoendoscopy and colon capsule panendoscopy. Suited to endoscopists and researchers interested in automated small bowel and colon reading.

title: Advanced Digestive Endoscopy: ERCP
author: Peter B. Cotton and Joseph Leung
summary: Thirteen chapters on endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography for endoscopists who already have basic skills. Early chapters cover the history of ERCP, training and competence assessment, technical fundamentals, and recording and reporting. Later chapters deal with bile duct stones and cholangitis, pancreaticobiliary malignancy, postsurgical bile leaks and strictures, sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, acute and chronic pancreatitis and their complications, ERCP in children, and the risks of the procedure with their prevention and management.

title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
subtitle: Diagnosis and Clinical Management
author: Anton Emmanuel and Eamonn M.M. Quigley
summary: An edited clinical guide to irritable bowel syndrome in four parts. The first covers definitions, Rome classification, epidemiology and global impact; the second deals with diagnosis, clinical assessment and the interface between primary and secondary care. The third, and largest, part treats symptoms one by one: self-management, food-related symptoms, gut inflammation, psychological factors, motility, visceral hypersensitivity and bloating, ending with a chapter on how to sequence treatments. A closing chapter looks at future diagnostic and therapeutic options. Suited to gastroenterologists, trainees and interested GPs.

title: Managing Complex Cases in Gastroenterology
subtitle: A Curbside Guide
author: W. Harley Sobin and Colleagues
summary: Over a hundred difficult cases are put to specialists at the Medical College of Wisconsin, written as a community gastroenterologist curbsiding academic colleagues. Four parts cover general GI (eosinophilic oesophagitis, achalasia, refractory GERD, Barrett's, PEG tubes, SIBO), an IBD compendium on refractory colitis, biologics and post-operative Crohn's, disorders of gut-brain interaction, and a hepatology compendium from abnormal liver tests to MASLD and alcoholic hepatitis. Each short chapter states the case, the question and the expert's practical answer, aimed at practising gastroenterologists, fellows and interested internists.

title: Lecture Notes: Gastroenterology and Hepatology
author: Anton Emmanuel and Stephen Inns
summary: A concise undergraduate text in five parts. Clinical basics cover the approach to abdominal pain, liver and luminal disease, nutrition, infections and investigations; a section on emergencies deals with GI bleeding, acute liver failure and acute pancreatitis. Regional chapters run from the oral cavity through oesophagus, stomach, bowel, colon, anorectum, pancreas and biliary tree to a full set of liver topics including viral, autoimmune, alcoholic and fatty liver disease, tumours, pregnancy and transplantation. It ends with revision aids such as history and examination routines, common OSCE cases and self-assessment case studies with answers.

title: Nutrition and Gastrointestinal Disease
author: Mark H. DeLegge
summary: A practical guide to nutrition support for gastroenterologists, from the Clinical Gastroenterology series. Thirteen chapters cover nutritional assessment and the effect of malnutrition on outcome, then nutrition in inflammatory bowel disease, liver failure, acute pancreatitis, coeliac disease, GI cancer, short bowel syndrome and obesity. The final chapters deal with enteral access and enteral feeding, parenteral nutrition, vascular access for parenteral nutrition and nutrition-based home care. It is intended as a hands-on reference for clinicians whose training included little formal nutrition teaching.

title: Neuro-Immuno-Gastroenterology
author: Cris S. Constantinescu and Colleagues
summary: An edited collection of 18 chapters on how the nervous system, the immune system and the gut interact. Opening chapters cover gut immunology, the enteric nervous system, the microbiota, substance P, VIP and stress. Later chapters look at Helicobacter pylori, gut microbiota and helminths in multiple sclerosis, Campylobacter and Guillain-Barré syndrome, neurological effects of anti-TNF drugs, gluten neurology, pernicious anaemia, Whipple's disease and gut dysfunction in multiple sclerosis. Written for gastroenterologists, neurologists and researchers working across both fields.

title: The Liver in Systemic Disease
subtitle: A Clinician’s Guide to Abnormal Liver Tests
author: Gideon M. Hirschfield and Colleagues
summary: What to do with an abnormal liver test when the patient was admitted for something else. After an opening chapter on the tests themselves, short take-home primers cover primary care and global practice, then the specialties where the question arises: intensive care, the postoperative patient, pregnancy, endocrinology, cardiac, respiratory, renal, skin, cancer, haematology and mental health. A closing section deals with prescribing, invasive procedures and drug-induced liver injury.

title: Cotton and Williams' Practical Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
subtitle: The Fundamentals
author: Catharine M. Walsh and Colleagues
summary: The trainee endoscopist's primer, now in its eighth edition, on how to pass the scope and what to do once it is in. Nine chapters cover the endoscopy unit and its staff, equipment and disinfection, consent, sedation and safety, then the practical craft of upper endoscopy and colonoscopy: handling the instrument, steering through the sigmoid, managing loops and removing polyps. ERCP, EUS and other advanced procedures get only a brief chapter, and a companion website of video clips carries the technique.

title: Pocket Handbook of GI Pharmacotherapeutics
author: Marianna G. Mavilia and George Y. Wu
summary: A pocket drug reference for gastrointestinal and liver disease, in 18 chapters covering reflux and peptic ulcer disease, GI bleeding, motility disorders, inflammatory bowel disease, GI infections, hepatitis, portal hypertension, cholestasis, hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, overload disorders, pruritus, post-liver transplant care, pancreatitis pain and pancreatic insufficiency. Each entry lists brand and generic names, indications, dosing, side effects, drug interactions, pregnancy and lactation concerns and a relative cost code, with treatment algorithms where available. Appendices cover the pregnancy labelling rule and abbreviations, and the index lists every drug alphabetically.

title: Principles of Clinical Gastroenterology
author: Tadataka Yamada
summary: A clinically oriented companion to Yamada's larger textbook, organised as 31 chapters that each describe the approach to a common presenting problem. Early chapters cover clinical decision making, economic analysis and psychosocial factors, followed by dyspepsia, dysphagia, reflux, peptic ulcer, overt and occult bleeding, colorectal cancer screening, weight loss, obesity, nausea, abdominal pain, acute abdomen, ileus, diarrhoea and constipation. Liver chapters deal with abnormal liver tests, jaundice, ascites, acute liver failure, chronic hepatitis B and C and liver masses, and the book closes with pregnancy, nutrition and genetic counselling.

title: Problem-based Approach to Gastroenterology and Hepatology
author: John N. Plevris and Colin W. Howden
summary: Eighteen chapters built around case scenarios, each followed by questions, a differential diagnosis, discussion and learning points from UK and US experts. Part One takes common presenting problems in gastroenterology: dysphagia, heartburn and atypical chest pain, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, upper GI and rectal bleeding, acute and chronic diarrhoea, and multisystem disease. Part Two covers pancreatobiliary disease, right upper quadrant pain, abnormal liver tests, acute and chronic liver disease, portal hypertension, liver infections, the transplant recipient and incidental radiological findings. Intended for trainees preparing for specialty postgraduate examinations.

title: Practical Gastroenterology and Hepatology
subtitle: Esophagus and Stomach
author: Nicholas J. Talley and Colleagues
summary: The oesophagus and stomach volume of a three-part series edited by Nicholas Talley with Kenneth DeVault and David Fleischer. Its 55 chapters run in seven parts: pathobiology, oesophagogastroduodenoscopy and its advanced techniques, other diagnostic tests such as motility testing, reflux monitoring and capsule endoscopy, and a problem-based approach to symptoms from heartburn and dysphagia to haematemesis. The remaining parts cover diseases of the oesophagus, including GORD, Barrett oesophagus, eosinophilic oesophagitis and cancer, diseases of the stomach, and functional disorders. A companion website holds procedure videos.

title: Practical Gastroenterology and Hepatology
subtitle: Liver and Biliary Disease
author: Nicholas J. Talley and Colleagues
summary: The liver and biliary volume of a three-volume set written for gastroenterology trainees and those preparing for certification. Its 36 short chapters move from liver anatomy and immunology through history taking, liver test interpretation, imaging, ERCP, EUS and liver biopsy, then take a problem-based approach to jaundice, liver masses, acute liver failure and portal hypertension. Later parts cover viral, metabolic, fatty, drug-induced, alcoholic, autoimmune and vascular liver disease, liver transplantation, and gallstones, sphincter of Oddi disorders, biliary cancer and strictures. Chapters open with an abstract, often include a clinical case and algorithms, and end with take-home points.

title: Pathogenesis and Clinical Practice in Gastroenterology
subtitle: Falk Symposium 160
author: I. Ferkolj and Colleagues
summary: Proceedings of Falk Symposium 160, held in Portorož, Slovenia, in June 2007, gathering 25 short review papers across luminal and liver disease. Sections cover dysphagia, reflux and Barrett's oesophagus, Helicobacter pylori, inflammatory bowel disease including the ECCO guidelines and biologics, coeliac disease, GI manifestations of AIDS, colorectal cancer screening and GI lymphoma. The liver sections deal with the role of liver biopsy, inflammation and cancer, the immunology and treatment of viral hepatitis, NASH, autoimmune and alcoholic hepatitis, PBC and PSC, hepatorenal syndrome, variceal bleeding and the surveillance, diagnosis and treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.
